name: rtty
label: RTTY (Baudot radioteletype)
description: RTTY (radioteletype) is the classic HF keyboard-to-keyboard mode: the 5-bit Baudot/ITA2 alphabet sent as 2-tone FSK. Amateur RTTY is almost universally 170 Hz shift at 45.45 baud — on the waterfall it's an unmistakable pair of parallel lines 170 Hz apart, flickering between mark and space. Decoded text streams under the decoder::fldigi log target (vendored fldigi RTTY core). Tune so the two tones straddle ~1500 Hz in the USB audio (dial ≈ signal − 1.5 kHz); AFC pulls in the rest. 20 m activity clusters 14.080–14.099 MHz; also 7.080–7.100, 21.080–21.100, 28.080–28.100, and 3.580–3.600 MHz. Weather/utility RTTY (e.g. DWD) runs 50 baud / 450 Hz shift — a different mode variant. Audio is teed alongside so you can listen.
ai_notes: RTTY (Baudot radioteletype, vendored fldigi core). Default rtty45 = 170 Hz shift / 45.45 baud / 5-bit Baudot — the amateur standard. Tune dial ≈ signal − 1500 Hz so the pair lands on fldigi's 1500 Hz sweetspot; AFC tracks. Amateur watering holes (USB): 3.590 / 7.090 / 14.085 / 21.090 / 28.090 MHz. Output: `tail decoder --category fldigi`. Weak/noisy copy is often the antenna/AGC, not the decoder — fixed gain + AGC off helps on quiet bands. Output is continuous (no slots): wait for a transmission, RTTY is bursty QSO/contest traffic.
